judge.name: openai-decisions
judge.confidence_method: P(chosen option), from the answer's per-option probabilities (yes/no: of the answer given)
judge.native_confidence: the API's `confidence` field, not defined by its documentation as P(chosen option); kept in raw as native_confidence, not audited
judge.price_note: documented base rate; regional and long-context multipliers are not applied

ground_truth.label: human-annotated
ground_truth.meaning: real items labelled by one annotator; annotator error is part of the ground truth
purpose: calibration and selective prediction per language on the same items
comparison between judges and between languages on parallel rows
caveats: translated parallel data, not native traffic; labels from SLURP annotation carried over by localisation
public since 2022: probably in the pretraining data of the judges audited

SLURP's utterances are requests to a home voice assistant collected for a research corpus, not production traffic; one intent label each, and MASSIVE publishes no inter-annotator agreement on the intent labels

localised from en-US by translators (FitzGerald et al. 2023 describe professional translators; the upstream card names each localiser by an obfuscated crowd-worker ID) and judged by three workers of the locale: 76 of 2974 rows have at least one of the localisation judges answering No to 'Does the sentence match the intent?', 0 a majority; _meta.intent_judgments keeps the scores (0 No, 1 Yes, 2 It is a reasonable interpretation of the goal)
options: the 60 MASSIVE intent identifiers in alphabetical order, without definitions; instructions in criteria.language (en) whatever the locale of the text

2944 distinct texts in 2974 rows (case and whitespace ignored); rows 12 and 248 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 28 and 656 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 41 and 1078 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 53 and 201 and 264 and 325 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 56 and 429 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 66 and 1043 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 132 and 457 and 465 and 519 and 757 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 159 and 975 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 244 and 301 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 262 and 724 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 310 and 914 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 388 and 2610 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 436 and 1054 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 452 and 560 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 495 and 689 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 528 and 529 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 554 and 988 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 609 and 837 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 618 and 795 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 695 and 1050 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 1221 and 1503 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 1835 and 1884 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 1878 and 1960 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 1971 and 1973 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 2363 and 2364 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label
